title: Artifact concurrency matrix
target: Artifact step-batch executor for one, five, and ten reports
contract: Task-output digest, step coverage, renderer-call count, shared-cap enforcement, and estimated cost remain unchanged.
summary: Added a deterministic scheduler matrix; no production worker configuration changed because no alternative proved faster across the supported batch sizes.
why_equivalent: Every profile invokes the real artifact step-batch executor for the same stage-one and distribution tasks; only worker and shared-slot limits vary.

checks.name: Full matrix outcomes
checks.detail: All 75 profile/batch results retained matching task digests, quality, rate caps, and zero estimated cost.

checks.name: Broader artifact suite
checks.detail: 35 passed and 1 failed in pre-existing unrelated dirty artifact-generation behavior.

workload: Three stage-one and two distribution tasks per report; one, five, and ten reports; every 1-5 worker and 1-5 shared-slot pair; two warmups and seven measured runs; deterministic 30 ms renderer latency.
limitations: The deterministic renderer proves scheduler and shared-slot behavior, not provider latency or artifact semantic generation.
residual_risks: A controlled live-provider canary is required before changing production model-concurrency limits.
The broader artifact suite currently has one unrelated failing test in a dirty production path.
notes: The fastest raw ten-report profile was 1x5, but its 0.96% median gain did not clear the 6.25% noise threshold and it is not suitable for single-report workload; the current 5x5 setting remains unchanged.
